title: Rev. Harold L. Webb & Rev. Thomas Miller v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Ministers complained that Pacific Presbytery conducted nonroutine business without the constitutionally required quorum of three teaching and three ruling elders. The Assembly agreed that the August 4, 1975 actions were irregular, but dismissed the complaint because Presbytery later met with a quorum and ratified those actions. The dismissal therefore reflected correction of the defect, not approval of proceeding without a quorum.

title: Session of Eastland Presbyterian Church, Memphis, Tennessee v. Covenant Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint found invalid because McKeown was not employed in a ministerial capacity
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A session complained that Covenant Presbytery violated PCA standards by approving the summer employment of a divorced and remarried man in a ministerial capacity. The Judicial Commission found the complaint invalid, holding that McKeown was not employed in a ministerial capacity. It expressly did not decide whether such employment would violate the Constitution. The General Assembly adopted the report as its action and judgment, leaving the presbytery's action undisturbed.

title: Session of Trinity Presbyterian Church, Slidell, Louisiana v. Grace Presbytery
disposition_detail: Case returned to lower court with instructions for new hearing; inadequate record
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The Session of Trinity Presbyterian Church, Slidell, Louisiana complained that Grace Presbytery violated proper procedure when it delayed the ordination of Adrian Pater, a licentiate who had been examined and sustained for ordination as an evangelist. The Judicial Commission found that inadequate minutes were presented and returned the matter to Grace Presbytery for a new hearing, while recommending that the General Assembly affirm that the BCO does not envision ordination expressly to pastoral services in churches of other denominations.

title: Rev. Paul L. Karlberg and Ruling Elder James G. Luce v. Central Georgia Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained; no substantive reason to remand after presbytery corrected and ended the commission's work
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Rev. Paul Karlberg and RE James Luce challenged Central Georgia Presbytery's handling of conflict at Faith Presbyterian Church, alleging that its commission had been biased and improperly constituted as a judicial commission. The Assembly's judicial commission did not sustain the complaint after the presbytery changed the body to a pastoral commission, rescinded most recommendations, and ended the investigation; it found no substantive reason to remand the matter.

title: John Kim v. Texas Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: John Kim appealed a decision of Texas Presbytery to the Judicial Commission. The Commission found Mr. Kim's explanation for his absence not satisfactory under BCO 43-10, and the case was deemed abandoned. The Commission voted 12-4 that the absence explanation was not satisfactory.

title: Rev. Thomas Barnes et al. v. Evangel Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained; written call requirement emphasized and broader question referred to the CJB
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The Fifth General Assembly approved its Judicial Commission’s refusal to sustain a complaint challenging Presbytery’s approval of Mercer for ordination as an evangelist without a call and for parachurch work outside its bounds. No reason for rejecting the complaint was stated. The ruling nevertheless required Presbytery to have—and itself issue—a written call before implementing the ordination decision, and requested referral of the broader question defining a valid ministerial call to the Permanent Committee on Judicial Business.

title: James H. Campbell v. Mid-Atlantic Presbytery
disposition_detail: New hearing ordered under BCO 44-5; judicial commission appointed for a potential further appeal
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: RE James Campbell challenged Mid-Atlantic Presbytery's approval of a commission report that rejected charges against Rev. Robert Schoof as inadmissible and limited the investigation. The Assembly directed the presbytery to hold a new hearing on the original charges under BCO 44-5, conform to the BCO, and keep the principals informed; it also appointed a judicial commission for any further appeal before the next Assembly.

title: Luther L. Allin, Jr., et al. (members of Session of Westminster Presbyterian Church) v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: Specifications of error sustained regarding lack of 10-day notice, improper participation by Wallace Bristow and Pastor Vitullo; specification regarding mandate of rotation system denied; matter remanded to Tennessee Valley Presbytery for hearing after proper notice
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Session members challenged Presbytery’s order to hold a congregational meeting on officer rotation and its handling of the complaint hearing. The Judicial Commission held that ten days ran from the notice’s postmark and that Bristow and Pastor Vitullo could not participate as members of the reviewing court. It nevertheless upheld Presbytery’s authority to require the meeting: a sufficient petition left the Session no option to refuse, while the congregation retained authority to decide rotation. The complaint was sustained in part and remanded for a properly noticed hearing.

title: Lockman v. Presbytery of Gulf Coast
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Victor E. Lockman appealed the October 13, 1979 action of the Presbytery of Gulf Coast; the Presbytery of Gulf Coast also submitted a reference requesting General Assembly make final disposition under BCO 42-3. The Committee recommended both be found in order and referred to a Judicial Commission appointed by the Eighth General Assembly with authority to make final disposition.

title: Rod Mays v. New River Presbytery
disposition_detail: Specification of error sustained 9-8; procedural failures identified
standard_of_review_detail: The commission identified procedural failures but did not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Rod Mays complained that New River Presbytery failed to address reported scandalous conduct by one of its ministers. The judicial commission sustained the specification of error by a 9-8 vote, explaining that required procedures concerning public offenses had not been followed, the responsible presbytery committee had not reported, and the proceedings had not been properly recorded.

title: Teaching Elders Byron Snapp and James M. Hope v. Calvary Presbytery
disposition_detail: Error sustained; ordination matter remanded to Calvary Presbytery for correction
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Teaching Elders challenged Calvary Presbytery’s use of the extraordinary clause to examine and ordain a candidate who had completed only one quarter of Hebrew. The Assembly sustained the complaint’s single specification because Presbytery had not demonstrated either extraordinary circumstances or the man’s proven extraordinary gifts. It found the ordination contrary to the Book of Church Order and remanded for correction. Rather than answer the broader question about proper use of the clause, it ordered a report to the Ninth General Assembly.

title: Teaching Elder Carl W. Bogue et al. v. Presbytery of the Ascension
disposition_detail: Both counts sustained (10-5 and 15-0); matter remanded for corrective action
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Complainants challenged Presbytery's sustaining of ordination trials for a candidate who affirmed continuing revelation through interpreted tongues and its approval of a campus-ministry call lacking required terms. The Assembly sustained both counts, holding that the examination left the candidate's views unclarified and failed adequately to protect the Standards' teaching on the finality and sufficiency of Scripture; Presbytery conceded the call's omission. It remanded the matter to obtain a BCO 21-1-compliant call and re-examine the candidate.

title: Ruling Elder Cooke Lewis, et al. v. Grace Presbytery
disposition_detail: Items 1–3 and the complaint as a whole not sustained; no BCO violation found
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Members of a congregation challenged Grace Presbytery's formation of an administrative commission, its method of appointing the commission, and its refusal to dissolve the pastoral relationship after a 26-16 congregational vote. The General Assembly adopted its Judicial Commission's judgment declining to sustain each item or the complaint as a whole because none of the challenged actions violated the BCO. It also urged all parties to continue efforts toward reconciliation.

title: Ruling Elder Robert H. Zeigler v. Presbytery of Texas
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A ruling elder complained that the Presbytery of Texas, handling a complaint against a session, appointed a committee rather than the requested commission and had that committee meet with the pastor, session members, and congregants before meeting the complainants. The Assembly adopted the Judicial Commission's report and unanimously confirmed the lower court's judgment (10-0). No adopted reasons or issue-level merits appear, so the case's value is a sparse example of a confirmed judgment without explanation.

title: Teaching Elder Rodney King, et al. v. Presbytery of Western Carolinas
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Complaint dated February 22, 1981, regarding certain actions of Texas Presbytery in handling a complaint brought by several members of North Dallas Presbyterian Church, Dallas, Texas. The Sub-Committee recommended the complaint not be received by the Ninth General Assembly as premature, since Texas Presbytery and North Dallas Church had not concluded the matter.

title: Stephen M. Lee, et al. v. Gulf Coast Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained in part; General Assembly instructed Gulf Coast Presbytery to re-examine Raymond Bradford Fell for ordination
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A Session challenged Gulf Coast Presbytery’s refusal to sustain Raymond Bradford Fell’s ordination examination, contending that his theonomic view was improperly treated as disqualifying and that prejudicial materials affected the process. The General Assembly sustained specifications 1, 2, and 5, but not 3 and 4. It ordered re-examination after direct guidance on specific biblical and confessional deficiencies, while expressly refusing to dictate the result. It also urged that no view of the judicial law’s present application should itself define orthodoxy or heresy.

title: Charles H. Davis, et al. v. Presbytery of Central Georgia
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; General Assembly sustained complaint against Presbytery for failing to sustain Davis's complaint about discipline matter
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The judicial commission sustained the complaints of Charles H. Davis and David H. Bryson against the Presbytery of Central Georgia for wrongfully failing to sustain Davis's complaint regarding Liberty Presbyterian Church's inadequate discipline of a member who obtained an unscriptural divorce on grounds of incompatibility.

title: David H. Bryson, et al. v. Presbytery of Central Georgia
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; same as Case 2 - General Assembly sustained complaint against Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Teaching elders challenged Central Georgia Presbytery’s refusal to sustain a complaint against Liberty Presbyterian Church’s Session for closing a disciplinary matter before taking judicial action. The General Assembly sustained the complaint, adopting findings that counseling, Session discussion, and instruction on discipline were underway before the Session closed the matter and refused to reopen it. It requested Presbytery to assist the Session with appropriate corrections or further action and said both courts should heed confessional teaching on marriage and repentance. The complainants’ requested affirmations were not expressly ordered.

title: Vaughn E. Hathaway, Jr., et al. v. Grace Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained conditionally; Western Carolinas Presbytery directed to proceed under BCO 32-3 and following
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Complainants challenged Grace Presbytery's refusal to ask the Assembly to assume original jurisdiction over allegations against a minister in Western Carolinas Presbytery. The Assembly did not sustain the complaint because Western Carolinas had not refused jurisdiction. It nevertheless directed that presbytery to proceed at its next stated meeting and held the one-year limitation inapplicable because its commission had unduly delayed formal process. The ruling was conditional, not an unqualified endorsement of the handling below.

title: James K. Workman, et al. (Session of Peace Presbyterian Church) v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; total-abstinence resolution held to bind conscience beyond Scripture
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The Session challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery’s refusal to rescind its resolution calling voluntary total abstinence from alcohol the proper Christian lifestyle. The General Assembly unanimously sustained the complaint, adopting the commission’s conclusion that the resolution in practice bound consciences and exceeded Scripture’s requirements contrary to the Westminster Confession. The judgment did not expressly rescind the resolution, and it distinguished improper conscience-binding from permissible teaching and counseling against alcohol abuse and intemperance.

title: Session of First Presbyterian Church, Stanley, North Carolina v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Mixed: Items 1, 2, and 5 of complaint sustained; Items 3, 4, and 6 not sustained. Assembly directed Presbytery to receive and hear complaints properly
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The Session challenged Presbytery’s refusal to receive complaints and associated voting, executive-session, elder-emeritus, interpretive, and disciplinary actions. The General Assembly sustained items 1, 2, and 5, but not 3, 4, and 6. Receiving a complaint under BCO 43-1 was not subject to a vote; when heard, complainants and respondents could not participate. Executive session was permissible, an elder emeritus retained full privileges, and item 6 was improper in this court. No reason was given for item 5. Presbytery was instructed to receive and hear the complaints properly.

title: Robert L. Reymond et al. v. Illiana Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained in all parts; case remanded for a new trial under proper BCO procedure
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Robert Reymond and others challenged Illiana Presbytery's handling of a teaching elder's confessed adultery and related violations, arguing that the presbytery reduced the charges and imposed a censure not commensurate with the offenses. The Assembly sustained the complaint in all parts, held that BCO 34-7 procedures and a more proportionate judgment were required, and remanded the case to Illiana Presbytery for a new trial.

title: Val H. Barleman et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; ordination-trial action annulled, with corrective and pastoral directions; protest recorded
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: RE Val Barleman and others challenged Ascension Presbytery's approval of Kurt Lutjens's ordination trials despite exceptions concerning admission to the Lord's Supper, baptism, Sabbath observance, baptism by immersion, and women serving as deacons. The Assembly sustained the complaint and annulled the presbytery's action sustaining the trials, while directing correction of the nonconforming portions and pastoral counsel; it did not itself annul the ordination or remove Lutjens from the presbytery roll, and a protest was recorded.

title: "Determined Minority" of New Life Presbyterian Church v. Judicial Commission of Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Items 2 and part of 5 sustained; Items 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7 not sustained
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Members of New Life Presbyterian Church challenged Central Carolina Presbytery's commission over its handling of membership dismissals and compliance with earlier Assembly directions. The General Assembly commission held that the presbytery commission exceeded BCO 57-5 membership requirements and sustained a related item in part, but did not sustain the remaining claims, including that the commission had failed to act or caused the entire conflict.

title: Stark Wilbor et al. v. North Georgia Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; action sustaining the transfer-license examination annulled; instruction and re-examination directed
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Complainants challenged North Georgia Presbytery’s approval of John Parrish’s transfer examination after he denied that the first day of the week is the Christian Sabbath. The General Assembly sustained the specification of error and annulled Presbytery’s action, characterizing the teaching as a fundamental element of doctrine. Presbytery was directed to instruct Parrish and, only if his view conformed to Scripture, the doctrinal standards, and the BCO, re-examine him in that area.

title: Jack Eubanks et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Items 2 and 3 sustained; Items 1, 4, and 5 not sustained
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Complainants challenged Presbytery’s called meeting and its actions concerning a judicial commission and church membership. The adopted adjudication sustained the objection to dissolving the commission by a 14–12 vote because Robert’s Rules required a two-thirds vote, and sustained without stated grounds the objection to ordering the dissolved commission to reassemble and revote. It rejected the challenges to the called meeting, Presbytery’s membership action, and its consideration of David Alexander’s complaint; the membership claim failed because church membership is not itself a court. No express remedy was ordered.

title: Session of Village Chapel Presbyterian Church v. Presbytery of Eastern Carolina
disposition_detail: Complaint abandoned for nonappearance under BCO 42-10; interim advice on Reference 8 confirmed
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The Session of Village Chapel challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery's decision to lift a matter from the table, alleging improper evidence and an accelerated decision. The Assembly's commission deemed the complaint abandoned when the complainant failed to appear after proper notice, and confirmed advice declining to answer questions that belonged in complaint or review proceedings while referring the remaining question to BCO 25-2.

title: David Lockwood Jr. and Evan Holyfield v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Item 4 sustained in part; Items 1, 2, 3, and 5 not sustained
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: David Lockwood Jr. and Evan Holyfield challenged Central Carolina Presbytery's commission for allegedly failing to act and mishandling discipline and reconciliation at New Life Presbyterian Church. The General Assembly commission rejected the failure-to-act claims, citing twenty-three meetings, and found that the complainants had not followed the reconciliation plan; it nevertheless sustained one overlapping membership-discipline item in part by reference to its ruling in Case 6.

title: Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC catalog records Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery as withdrawn before a merits decision. No opinion text has been located in the local case corpus.

title: Jack Eubanks et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Items 1–3 sustained; judgment on Item 4 reserved
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Complainants challenged a called Presbytery meeting and its actions concerning a judicial commission and church membership. The adjudication sustained objections to dissolving the commission by a 14–12 vote and ordering the dissolved commission to reconvene and revote. A commission with power could be dismissed only by a two-thirds vote under Robert’s Rules; no separate ground was stated for the reconvening issue. Challenges to the meeting, Presbytery’s membership action, and its receipt of another complaint were not sustained. No relief was specified.

title: Donald A. Codling et al. v. Presbytery of Eastern Canada
disposition_detail: Specifications 1, 4, 5, and 6 sustained; specifications 2 and 3 not sustained; re-examination urged
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Presbytery members challenged Eastern Canada Presbytery’s denial of Ron Harris’s licensure. The complaint was sustained regarding the improperly adopted supermajority rule and the insufficiency of objections concerning counseling, evangelistic preaching, and sovereign grace; claims that pertinent data was excluded and requests to hear Harris preach were blocked were not sustained. Citing the fragmented examination and sharply differing views, the Assembly urged a complete reexamination at one meeting. It did not order Harris licensed or formally remand the matter.

title: RE Truman Swain et al. v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint abandoned; no merits judgment located
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: RE Truman Swain and others brought a complaint against Eastern Carolina Presbytery. The official SJC catalog records the matter as abandoned, with no merits judgment published in the available record.

title: W. Ted Smith Jr. v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained as improperly framed; matter treated as a protest, with substance addressed in related cases
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE W. Ted Smith complained that Central Carolina Presbytery failed to carry out Assembly and presbytery directives concerning restoration and oversight of members of New Life Presbyterian Church and asked for dissolution of the pastor's pastoral relationship and censure. The Assembly did not sustain the complaint because it was not properly a complaint but appeared to be a protest, while noting that much of its substance had been addressed in related cases and directing a broader response to the New Life conflict.

title: Elder Roy J. Wuckovich v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: complaint not sustained; lower court decision confirmed
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The Committee on Judicial Business found Case 1, a complaint by RE Roy Y. Wuckovich against Central Carolina Presbytery, to be in order and recommended that a judicial commission be elected to adjudicate the matter. No full case report appears in this window; only the listing and brief recommendation are present.

title: Russell D. Toms and TE William L. Thompson v. Central Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: specification of error sustained; matter referred back to presbytery for proper procedures
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The Committee on Judicial Business found Case 2, a complaint by TE Russell D. Toms et al. against the Presbytery of Central Florida, to be in order and recommended that a judicial commission be elected to adjudicate the matter. No full case report appears in this window; only the listing and brief recommendation are present.

title: McLeod v. Gulf Coast Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Case 3, an appeal by RE George K. McLeod against Gulf Coast Presbytery, was found not in order because the appellant was no longer a member of the Presbyterian Church in America; his church voted to withdraw from the PCA on December 17, 1983.

title: Carl W. Bogue, et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension
disposition_detail: Continued non-compliance and constitutional violation sustained 12-3; contumacy not sustained 1-14; remedial recommendations adopted
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Ascension Presbytery was challenged for resolving not to comply with prior General Assembly directions concerning an ordination examination. The case was sustained as to continued noncompliance and constitutional violation, but not as to contumacy; remedial recommendations were adopted. The supplied text contains the complaint rather than the operative judgment, so it does not disclose the adjudicative reasoning or the specific remedial measures.

title: Robert C. Peterson, et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension
disposition_detail: specifications of continued non-compliance and constitutional violation sustained; recommendations for remedial action adopted
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Complaint challenged Ascension Presbytery's March 10, 1984 refusal to obey the Eleventh General Assembly's directive to correct constitutional defects in Kurt Lutjens's ordination trial, and its purported BCO 41 reference of the matter to the Twelfth General Assembly for retrial. The CJB sustained specifications of continued non-compliance and constitutional violation and adopted recommendations for remedial action. The complaint's asserted distinction—that BCO 41 cannot return a prior General Assembly decision for retrial—marks the case's practical limit.

title: Warren Gardner, et al. v. Presbytery of North Georgia
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Case 6, a complaint by TE Warren Gardner et al. against North Georgia Presbytery, is listed in Supplement A of the CJB report. A recommendation (72) was made but its text does not appear in this window.

title: Session of Faith Presbyterian Church, Akron, Ohio, et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension
disposition_detail: Continued non-compliance sustained 15-0; constitutional violation not sustained 5-8-2; contumacy not sustained 0-13-2; remedial recommendations adopted
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A Session and other complainants challenged Presbytery’s May 1984 resolution as continued noncompliance with directions from an earlier ordination case. The continued-noncompliance specification was sustained, but allegations of constitutional violation and contumacy were not sustained. Remedial recommendations were adopted, although the supplied excerpt provides neither their terms nor the deciding body’s reasons. The mixed ruling therefore distinguishes noncompliance from the complainants’ more serious characterizations of Presbytery’s conduct.

title: Session of Faith Presbyterian Church, Akron, Ohio v. Ascension Presbytery
disposition_detail: Motion to find the complaint in order ruled out of order; moderator's ruling sustained by the Assembly
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The Session of Faith Presbyterian Church complained against Ascension Presbytery's alleged failure to comply with earlier Assembly directions concerning Kurt Lutjens. Although the Committee on Judicial Business recommended finding the complaint in order, the moderator ruled that motion out of order, and the Thirteenth General Assembly sustained the ruling; a dissent objected that the complaint had been timely filed.

title: Charges from Eastern Canada Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Charges referred to the General Assembly for adjudication from Eastern Canada Presbytery were denied as not in order because the accused parties had renounced the jurisdiction of the PCA by joining another church (BCO 38-4).

title: Watterson v. General Assembly et al
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: A complaint by RE Gene Watterson against the General Assembly was found not in order on two grounds: the presbytery had not yet acted on the relevant commission report at the date of the alleged complaint (BCO 43-1), and even if the presbytery accepted the report, the complaint must first be dealt with by the presbytery before coming to the Assembly.

title: Mayfield v. Siouxlands Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal found not in order as untimely under BCO 42-4
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The Assembly found Jack Mayfield's appeal not in order under BCO 42-4 because he filed it nearly a year and a half after the matter had been adjudicated, and his reasons did not justify disregarding the filing requirement. The ruling did not reach the underlying merits and directed him instead to BCO 37-4's procedure for removing censure.

title: S. Michael Preg, Jr., et al. v. Missouri Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Complaint by Westminster Reformed Presbyterian Church session against Missouri Presbytery for establishing a standing committee to conduct required annual visitations to member churches. Commission sustained the complaint, finding that presbytery exceeded its constitutional authority under BCO 13-9 to require visits without expressed provision or grounds in the BCO.

title: Gentry et al. v. Calvary Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Commission elected to adjudicate complaint of TE Kenneth L. Gentry, Jr. et al. vs. Calvary Presbytery. Commission recommended that the assembly's action in finding the complaint in order and electing the commission be reconsidered. Assembly adopted the recommendation, rescinded the original determination, and found the complaint not in order, thus disestablishing the commission.

title: Kenneth L. Gentry, Jr. et al. v. Calvary Presbytery
disposition_detail: Sustained - Calvary Presbytery erred in sustaining Mr. Hyer's examination; verdict annulled and remanded to presbytery for pastoral counseling and re-examination
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Ministers challenged Calvary Presbytery's approval of William Hyer's examination and reception despite his belief that noncanonical, nonbinding revelation could continue. The Assembly sustained the complaint because PCA standards foreclose continuing revelation beyond illumination and providence. It annulled only the examination portion concerning revelation, suspending his reception, and instructed Presbytery to counsel and re-examine him, then report to the next Assembly. The majority deemed the record sufficient despite a dissent emphasizing Hyer's affirmation of Scripture's finality and the absence of an examination transcript.

title: Vaughn E. Hathaway, Jr. et al. v. Grace Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained - Commission voted not to sustain complaint on grounds of no explicit constitutional guidance on divorce and remarriage
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The Committee on Judicial Business found Case 2, the complaint of TE Hathaway et al. against the Presbytery of Grace, to be in order and recommended that a commission be appointed to adjudicate the matter.

title: Henry D. Knight, Jr. v. Palmetto Presbytery
disposition_detail: Mixed - Specifications 1 and 3 sustained, specs 2 and 4 not sustained. Matter remanded to Palmetto Presbytery for new hearing on specs 1 and 3
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A ruling elder challenged Palmetto Presbytery’s publication, as an appendix to meeting minutes, of a letter never discussed at that meeting, and its handling of his complaint. The Judicial Commission sustained specifications 1 and 3: Presbytery had not clearly declared the publication erroneous, and it risked harming Covenant’s Session. Specifications 2 and 4 failed because Presbytery timely referred the complaint, though its record was inaccurate, and acted in good faith. Despite Presbytery’s later deletion of the letter, the Commission remanded for a new hearing on specifications 1 and 3.

title: Edward A. Steele III v. Great Lakes Presbytery
disposition_detail: Abandoned - Case found abandoned as no one appeared to represent the appeal
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The Committee on Judicial Business found Case 4, the appeal of TE Steele against the Presbytery of Great Lakes, to be in order and recommended that a commission be appointed; a constitutional inquiry was appended regarding whether the appellant's divestiture from office was suspended pending the commission's action.

title: D. Keith Abee et al. v. James River Presbytery
disposition_detail: All six specifications sustained on grounds of procedural deficiencies. Censures reversed and remanded to presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Five appellants challenged censures imposed after a Presbytery commission treated a Session's request for assistance as authority to initiate judicial process. The Assembly sustained all six specifications, holding that the commission lacked authority to proceed before charges were approved and that original jurisdiction remained with the Session. title: Stuart Merriam v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery (Appeal)
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: After Tennessee Valley Presbytery deposed a minister without conducting a church trial, he appealed, alleging denial of PCA due process. The SJC remanded for a new trial. It held that Presbytery could bring charges but could not substitute the Papua New Guinea criminal proceedings for ecclesiastical process, especially when it neither served an indictment and charges nor appointed counsel for an accused unable to attend. The remand permitted a constitutionally compliant trial; it did not resolve guilt or bar discipline.

It found no proof that Blaha’s denial that the gifts conveyed revelation crossed prior Assembly limits and deferred to Presbytery on an unsettled issue. It expressly declined reexamination or remand; a substantial partial dissent would have set the examination aside.

title: Linton v. Western Carolina Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: An elder challenged Presbytery’s failure to interview accusers, alleged investigative delay, and resulting finding of no strong presumption of a pastor’s guilt. The SJC denied the complaint. The ordinary stated-meeting sequence used here disclosed no clear constitutional error. The SJC therefore deferred to Presbytery’s superior proximity to the facts and upheld its finding.

title: Lyons v. Western Carolina Presbytery

summary: Lyons challenged Presbytery’s investigation of accusations against a teaching elder, alleging failure to interview accusers, undue delay, and an erroneous finding of no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC denied the complaint and additionally held that Lyons lacked standing because he was not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. The consolidated opinion explained that BCO 31-2 requires due diligence but prescribes neither interviews nor a timeline; finding no constitutional or clear factual error, it deferred to Presbytery’s judgment.

title: Woodward v. Western Carolina Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Robert Woodward challenged Presbytery’s acceptance of a finding that accusations against TE Craig Bulkeley did not raise a strong presumption of guilt, alleging investigators never heard his evidence. The SJC denied the complaint, specifically holding that Woodward lacked standing because he was not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. It also held that BCO 31-2 prescribes no interview requirement or fixed timeline and found no clear constitutional error warranting departure from ordinary deference to Presbytery.

title: Complaint TE Larry Edison, et. al. v. Southwest Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Ministers complained that Southwest Florida Presbytery improperly reexamined Bryan Gregory and reversed his examination, membership, and call after previously receiving him. The SJC upheld Presbytery’s authority to hear and sustain the earlier complaint but sustained the present complaint on the remedial actions. Sustaining a complaint did not itself undo prior acts; once Presbytery had treated Gregory as a member, his membership rights could be removed only through disciplinary due process. The SJC annulled the reexamination and March 24 actions and directed Presbytery to consider appropriate remedies. Gregory’s theology was not before it.

title: Armes v. Southwest Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Presbytery refused to hear Armes’s complaint against his excommunication, initially reasoning that excommunication deprived him of standing and later ruling the complaint untimely. Presbytery conceded its error on the standing ground, and all parties stipulated to remand for a hearing. The SJC confirmed that stipulation, sustained the complaint, and remanded the case without deciding the validity of the excommunication itself.

standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.

The judgment deliberately left unresolved whether any of the six views themselves were faithful to the Constitution; the detailed view-by-view analysis appeared only in a concurring opinion.

title: Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.

Although a presbytery may dismiss charges under BCO 29-1, 32-20, 34-2, or 31-8, it bears the burden of documenting that basis; KEP did not. The SJC refused Lee's request that it enter the guilt verdicts the presbytery should have reached—that power exists on appeal, not complaint. It remanded for KEP to begin process under BCO 32.

title: Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed Matt Ruff's complaint against Nashville Presbytery as judicially out of order under OMSJC 10.5.a. Ruff challenged Presbytery's failure to investigate a teaching elder, but BCO 43 requires a complaint against an act or decision; lack of action qualifies only when a court meeting has occurred and the court failed to act. Presbytery's nearest antecedent meeting was August 18, 2010, and Ruff filed October 27, 2010, beyond BCO 43-2's thirty-day limit. Because the defect could not be cured, the case was dismissed without reaching the merits; a separate objection disputed that ruling.

It declined to require reordination, calling that question unsettled and treating BCO 37-5’s restoration pronouncement as sufficient pending clarification. The SJC annulled Presbytery’s actions concerning the minister and remanded for a proper probationary and review process.

title: Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery (Cases 2011-11, 2011-12, 2011-15, 2011-16)
disposition_detail: Complaint denied; pastoral restriction and lower-court judgment affirmed
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Hahn challenged Presbytery’s ruling that CTKPC Session lawfully excluded him from that congregation’s worship until a psychiatric evaluation addressed safety concerns. The SJC denied the complaint. Applying BCO 39-3.3, it found no clear error in the lower courts’ credibility and discretionary judgments, given Session’s familiarity with the people and events. It characterized the restriction as informal pastoral safety guidance, not judicial discipline: it did not bar sacraments, worship elsewhere, or transfer, and attendance could resume upon medical assurance. The conditional local restriction therefore remained undisturbed.

title: Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West. (also Cases 2011-11 and 2011-15)
disposition_detail: Appeal denied; disciplinary judgment affirmed because no clear error was shown
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Hahn appealed Presbytery’s guilty judgment and indefinite suspension from the sacraments, alleging trial irregularities, denial of a requested amendment, haste, and prejudice. The SJC denied the appeal on all three charges: false and unsubstantiated accusations, disobedience and disrespect toward church authorities, and a bitter and malignant spirit. Applying BCO 39-3.3, it deferred to Presbytery’s familiarity with the parties, witnesses, and extensive trial record and found no clear error, even though contrary evidence may have existed. The judgment and censure therefore remained undisturbed.
