standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Keating challenged Warrior Presbytery’s decision to divest him of ordination without censure while he was absent. The SJC sustained his appeal, reversed and voided the divestiture, and remanded because BCO 34-10’s required opportunity to be heard in his defense was not provided; this also amounted to hurrying before all testimony was taken. It rejected the reasonable-indulgence claim because Presbytery did not know of his postponement request. Keating remained a minister in good standing, but Presbytery could reconsider divestiture after reasonably soliciting a defense.

title: Charles Tarter v. Evangel Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained; judgment and censure vacated and matter remanded for constitutionally compliant proceedings or dismissal
standard_of_review_detail: The SJC expressly applied BCO 39-3.3: it owed great deference to the lower court on matters of discretion and judgment, but held that the judicial commission clearly erred in its judgment.
summary: A teaching elder appealed his judgment and deposition for refusing Presbytery committee directives and allegedly avoiding accountability. The SJC sustained five of nine specifications, holding that the committee could not impose requirements lacking constitutional warrant or control an independent mission board; vague allegations and testimony unavailable for cross-examination also impaired the trial. Because the record did not prove an ongoing pattern of insubordination, it vacated the censure and remanded for a constitutionally compliant proceeding or dismissal. Three specifications failed, while one duplicated another.

title: Dunn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found TE Dwight Dunn's complaint against Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery to be administratively out of order because the complaint was transmitted to a presbytery commission by the Stated Clerk rather than by motion and action of Presbytery, and because the commission's judgment was never brought back to Presbytery for approval as required by BCO 15-3.

title: Hedman v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: RE Gerald Hedman complained that Pacific Northwest Presbytery unconstitutionally adopted five not-guilty verdicts regarding TE Peter Leithart's teachings on baptism, covenants, imputation, justification, and union with Christ. The SJC denied the complaint, finding it was bound by the Record of the Case and that Complainant had not demonstrated clear error on the part of Presbytery, with concurring and dissenting opinions discussing the scope of review, standing, and concerns about Leithart's sacramental theology.

title: Bethel v. Southeast Alabama Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled Case 2012-06 administratively out of order on two grounds: the complaint was not filed within the required 30-day period under BCO 43-2, and the complainant (a deacon who was not a commissioner to presbytery on the date of the action complained against) lacked standing under BCO 43-1.

title: William G. Mitchell v. The Presbytery of the Ascension
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.4: the higher court interprets and applies the Church Constitution according to its best ability, without the same deference to the lower court.
summary: A ruling elder appealed judgments concerning an alleged broken promise to take a sabbatical and deficient performance as Session clerk. Because the pivotal email was absent from the record, the SJC vacated the sabbatical-related judgment and remanded for Presbytery only to consider whether a new trial was warranted. It reversed and dismissed the clerk-duty specification because the four-month delay in submitting minutes was attributable to the Session and did not justify a trial. Only the first specification remained potentially triable.

title: Complaint: TE Art Sartorius v. Siouxlands Presbytery 2013-03 Complaint: Mr. G. Rick Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery 2013-06 Appeal: TE Stephen Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery 2013-08 Complaint of
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Teaching and ruling elders challenged Presbytery’s approval of TE Gregory Lawrence’s acquittal on five doctrinal charges. The SJC sustained the complaint on procedural grounds: the trial commission relied on his post-indictment exculpatory writings while he declined to testify, depriving the prosecution of cross-examination. The SJC ordered a new trial on the same indictment under specified evidentiary procedures. Because this was a complaint rather than an appeal, it did not reverse the acquittals into findings of guilt or decide the doctrinal merits.
topic_tags: rules of evidence in ecclesiastical courts

title: Bennett v. Missouri Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled Case 2012-09 administratively out of order because, although the complainant was a PCA member when he filed his original complaint to Presbytery on April 16, 2012, he had transferred to the OPC on April 28, 2012, and therefore lacked standing to bring his complaint to the SJC on August 16, 2012.

title: PCA v. Korean Capital Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The 40th General Assembly had cited Korean Capital Presbytery for failure to respond to exceptions of substance in minutes from October 6, 2008. The SJC noted that Korean Capital Presbytery submitted responses approved by the Presbytery under BCO 10-4, and found those responses acceptable.

title: Dunn and Pesnell v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Dunn and TE Pesnell complained that Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery erred in adopting its commission's recommendation to institute process and proceed to trial against TE David Swavely for alleged pastoral and spiritual abuse. The SJC denied the complaint, finding that the Presbytery had sufficient authority to proceed to trial and that the errors alleged did not rise to a reversible level.

title: Jackson v. Northwest Georgia
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Case 2013-02 (RE Warren Jackson vs. Northwest Georgia Presbytery) was found to be Administratively Out of Order by the Standing Judicial Commission. No substantive decision on the merits was reached.

title: Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Marshall complained that Pacific Presbytery wrongly refused to dismiss a judicial case despite alleged procedural irregularities in the indictment and process. The SJC held the complaint judicially out of order: objections arising in a judicial case were to be preserved for appeal under BCO 32-14 and 42-3, and Marshall’s pending appeal independently barred a complaint under BCO 43-1. It granted no complaint relief. Separate opinions disputed the first rationale but agreed that the pending appeal barred the complaint.

title: the Session of Hope Community Church v. Central Carolina Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Hope Community Church’s Session challenged Presbytery’s requirement that a multi-site congregation eventually particularize its second worship site. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled the requirement, and struck it from the Presbytery Manual because BCO 12-5e specifically entrusts the time and place of worship to the Session, which Presbytery’s general church-enlargement authority could not supersede. The narrow ruling did not resolve broader concerns about multi-site churches or eliminate Presbytery’s review of a second site’s location under BCO 13-9(g).
topic_tags: session authority over time and place of worship

title: Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
disposition_detail: Administratively out of order; request to assume original jurisdiction not heard
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Mr. Stephen Hahn asked the Standing Judicial Commission to assume original jurisdiction over Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery. The SJC found the request administratively out of order and so did not reach a merits review. The report states no reason for the ruling and identifies no underlying dispute, leaving only the disposition itself.

title: Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A minister appealed Great Lakes Presbytery’s divestiture of his office without censure under BCO 34-10. The SJC sustained his claim that Presbytery failed to make required findings that he habitually neglected official functions and that any neglect arose only from lack of acceptance to the Church. It reversed and annulled the divestiture, leaving him a member in good standing, and required no further action. The other four specifications were moot. Presbytery remained free to pursue proper Chapter 31 process or a procedurally compliant BCO 34-10 divestiture.
topic_tags: lack of acceptance to the Church
habitual failure to perform official functions

title: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port v. Presbytery of Southwest Florida
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC sustained the Session of FPC North Port's complaint that Southwest Florida Presbytery erred when it remanded a previously out-of-order complaint back to the Session and when it directed and instructed the Session to initiate formal ecclesiastical process against a member without following the required steps of BCO 40-5. The Commission held that once the Original CM Complaint was found out of order, there was no matter for Presbytery to carry forward, and any subsequent instructions to the Session to initiate process were null and void.

title: Jackson v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Jackson challenged Northwest Georgia Presbytery’s failure to act on his BCO 40-5 letter alleging delinquency by Midway’s Session. The SJC found his complaint administratively out of order and dismissed it because he was not a commissioner at Presbytery’s January 2013 meeting; originating a BCO 40-5 report did not confer standing. Separately, the SJC accepted jurisdiction over Presbytery’s failure to respond and remitted the matter for constitutional disposition, without deciding whether the Session committed the alleged delinquencies.

title: Marshall v. Pacific
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Appeal by Mr. G. Rick Marshall vs. Pacific Presbytery. Case was withdrawn as prematurely filed and therefore did not proceed to a full SJC decision.

title: Latimer v. Chicago Metro Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: The SJC sustained Rev. Latimer's appeal from his deposition for allegedly pursuing an unbiblical divorce, finding that Presbytery clearly erred because the record contained no conclusive evidence that his divorce filing — made on advice of counsel to protect his children — reflected an intent to divorce rather than a defensive legal measure; two concurring opinions addressed the Presbytery's choice of definite versus indefinite suspension.

title: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port, Florida v. Presbytery of Southwest Florida
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A Session appealed Presbytery’s judgment finding it guilty and suspending it for refusing instructions to institute process against a member. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversed the judgment in whole, and dismissed the charges. Once Presbytery denied the member’s complaint, that matter should have ended; moreover, Presbytery did not follow BCO 40-4’s required first step before invoking BCO 40-5 review and control. The delay, prejudice, and missing-witness specifications were moot. The decision did not fault Presbytery’s underlying concern.

title: Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed the appeal and suspended the lower court's judgment indefinitely because Pacific Presbytery failed to transmit a material part of the Record of the Case — a defect that could not be remedied — and rebuked the Presbytery for failure to preserve and transmit trial testimony.

title: Aven and Dively v. Ohio Valley Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Two ministers complained that Ohio Valley Presbytery erred in granting TE Hickey an exception to Larger Catechism 177 regarding admission of covenant children to the Lord's Supper. The SJC neither sustained nor denied the complaint, remanding the case to the Presbytery because the record was insufficient to evaluate the minister's particular expression of his paedocommunion view.
topic_tags: fundamentals of the system of doctrine

title: Sanfacon v. Philadelphia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: An inactive ruling elder's complaint to the Session was filed 78 days after the Session action complained against, exceeding the 60-day window of BCO 43-2. The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order and voided all subsequent actions.

title: Gearhart v. Chicago Metro Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: An unsigned complaint was filed on TE Gearhart's behalf by a third party without standing, and TE Gearhart did not contact the PCA Clerk until 77 days after the Presbytery action (47 days past the BCO 43-3 deadline). The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order because it was not timely filed and the complainant did not give unqualified ratification.

title: Flesher and Weekly v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found Complaint 2015-03 moot because the issues it raised were adjudicated in the related Appeal 2015-08 (Hardie v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery).

title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Thompson used a BCO 43 complaint to challenge his Session indictment during an ongoing disciplinary case, according to the separate concurrence. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order. It held that a defendant must raise such objections during process in the court of original jurisdiction under BCO 32-14 and, if still dissatisfied, pursue them on appeal under BCO 42-3. The ruling did not decide the indictment objection’s merits.

title: Application of Thompson v. South Florida
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: A BCO 40-5 application to cite Granada Presbyterian Church for alleged grossly unconstitutional proceedings and discipline delinquencies was found administratively out of order and dismissed as prematurely filed. The SJC held that, even assuming a credible report, BCO 40-5 first required citing the offending court before South Florida Presbytery, the court of appellate jurisdiction. Because Presbytery had docketed the matter for its August 11, 2015 meeting and had not yet ruled, the SJC could not act. No merits ruling on the discipline allegations was made.

title: Presbyterian Church in America v. South Florida Presbytery (Citation)
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Reviewing South Florida Presbytery’s response to a General Assembly citation, the SJC found most responses satisfactory but rejected one because it did not address BCO 32-2’s requirement to proceed once a charge is made. It approved previously unsubmitted 2009 executive-session minutes with an exception because their treatment of a teaching elder appeared to violate BCO 46-8. Presbytery also had to submit amended minutes and complete, or formally plan, overdue Session-record reviews for report to the 45th General Assembly.
topic_tags: citation for failure to respond to exceptions

title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Thompson's complaint to the SJC was prematurely filed before South Florida Presbytery had considered it at its next stated meeting as required by BCO 43-2. The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order.

title: Hardie v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: TE John Hardie appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension by Metro Atlanta Presbytery's judicial commission, raising seventeen specifications of error under six categories including procedural irregularities, improper evidence, refusal of indulgence, prejudice, and disproportionate censure. The SJC denied the appeal, finding no clear error in MAP's proceedings and upholding the indefinite suspension.

title: Bumgarner v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Bumgarner, a ruling elder who had been deposed in 2012, filed a BCO 40-5 application in 2015 seeking reversal of the censure after having previously withdrawn his complaint and acknowledged it could not be resubmitted. The SJC dismissed the application as administratively out of order because it sought to re-file a withdrawn complaint and because BCO 40-3 prohibits reversal of judicial censures except by appeal or complaint.

title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed a BCO 40-5 application because the matter concerned proceedings in a judicial case in which a complaint had been filed. Under BCO 40-3, such proceedings may not be handled by review and control once notice of appeal or complaint is given to the lower court. The SJC therefore found the case administratively out of order and not capable of being put in order under OMSJC 9.1.a., and dismissed it under OMSJC 9.2(d).

title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: After a Session excommunicated a member without trial for contumacy, the SJC sustained his complaint and annulled the contumacy judgment, excommunication, and later Session and Presbytery actions. No mutually agreed BCO 38-1 confession existed, and declining a confession meeting was not immediately censurable objective contumacy under BCO 32-6; subjective contumacy required confession or trial. He reverted to membership under pending indictment. The SJC did not find the indictment unconstitutional, decide trial guilt, or consider the unpleaded trespass warning.

title: Wills v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled Wills's complaint against MAP's September 15, 2015 action declaring a prior complaint administratively out of order was itself administratively out of order, because BCO 43-2 requires a complaint to first be made to the court whose act is alleged to be in error, and MAP had not yet had the opportunity to respond; Duncan, Evans, and Donahoe dissented.

title: Barnes v. Heartland Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Heartland Presbytery sustained the transfer of TE Geoff Smith from an OPC presbytery with stated differences on WCF 19 (the law), without adequately considering or disclosing to the full presbytery that the OPC had declared Smith's views outside the system of doctrine and had restricted him from teaching them. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded to Heartland for further action, with a dissent arguing there was no clear error under BCO 39-3(3).
topic_tags: fundamentals of the system of doctrine

title: Aven v. Ohio Valley Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: An SJC complaint alleged that Ohio Valley Presbytery failed to comply with the SJC's prior remand in Case 2014-01, which required it to 'hear further' from TE Charles Hickey about his changed view on Larger Catechism 177. The SJC denied the complaint. It held that the prior decision neither sustained nor denied the original complaint and prescribed no particular examination procedure; Hickey's nine pages of additional affirmations, exegesis, and answers constituted hearing further, and he addressed the five identified areas at least in part. A concurrence believed the SJC could also have adjudicated the confessional-difference merits; a dissent would have found noncompliance and reached the merits.
topic_tags: fundamentals of the system of doctrine

title: Robertstad v. North Texas Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order because it was initially filed via e-mail rather than by hard copy, and was filed by hard copy only after the thirty-day deadline had passed, contrary to BCO 43-3 and OMSJC 18.10.b which prohibit e-mail filing. A concurring opinion provided extensive history of the 2012 and 2014 amendments to BCO 43-3.

title: Troxell v. Presbytery of the Southwest
disposition_detail: Complaint partially sustained; challenged action annulled
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A complaint challenged Presbytery’s institution of two charges against a teaching elder and related pretrial actions. The SJC annulled the household-management charge because process began fifteen months after the alleged offense and the record showed no recently flagrant, newly evident, or continuing offense under BCO 32-20. It also held that declaring the elder not in good standing removed rights without process, but left his properly imposed suspension effective. It rejected objections to discussion, questioning, and the timely submission charge, which could proceed without any determination of guilt.

title: Avery and Lewelling v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Avery and Lewelling complained against Nashville Presbytery's denial of their complaint about the Shepherding Committee's investigation of TE Jim Bachmann. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order because the actions complained of were those of a committee rather than a court, and the complaint against November 2015 Presbytery action was untimely under BCO 43-2.

title: Doty v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Ms. Doty and 21 others filed charges against a Nashville Presbytery teaching elder first with his congregation's Session (wrong court), then with Nashville Presbytery; Presbytery declined to indict and treated the matter as a report under BCO 31-2 rather than charges. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order (11-9-2-2) on the ground that Doty lacked standing under BCO 43-1 as a non-member of Nashville Presbytery; a significant dissent argued that her filing of charges gave her standing under prior precedent (Lyons, Ruff, Fordice).

title: Fordice v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: A church member challenged Presbytery’s denial of his complaint after it resolved accusations against a minister through a BCO 38-1 confession rather than trial. The SJC held that using confession without process was not itself error, but the statement and confession failed to correlate with and address the specific allegations. It sustained the complaint, annulled the denial, and remanded for Presbytery to amend the documents, institute process, reactivate the investigative committee, or otherwise respond directly and specifically to the unresolved allegations.

title: Korean Northwest Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC approved a motion to accept Korean Northwest Presbytery's amended and corrected responses to exceptions on a roll-call vote; Neikirk dissented and Dowling abstained, with three members absent. The amended responses therefore stand accepted. The source supplies no underlying exception content or reasons, so the action is a procedural acceptance rather than a merits ruling.

title: Frazier v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC denied a complaint challenging Nashville Presbytery's decision not to indict a teaching elder for allegedly sinful teaching on homosexuality and same-sex attraction. The adopted judgment held that the 147-page record showed Presbytery fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duty and did not show it erred in judgment when it declined process; the complaint was denied 20-0-1. Concurring opinions raised concerns about committee recusal, record clarity, and exegetical uses of Scripture, but they were separate and did not alter the denial.

title: Harwell et al. v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed this complaint as judicially out of order because the Harwell complainants had not first properly filed a complaint with Nashville Presbytery—what they filed with Presbytery was in fact a suggestion of charges or call for investigation under BCO 31-2, not a complaint against a court action—and then filed their SJC complaint directly, bypassing the required step of complaining first to the court whose action is alleged to be in error.

title: Daniels et al. v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC declared the complaint moot by a vote of 13-6; the substantial dissenting opinion by six members argued the Commission provided no rationale for the mootness determination and that no constitutional basis for declaring it moot was established.

title: Wills v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue 1 applies BCO 39-3.4 to constitutional interpretation; Issue 2 applies BCO 39-3.3 to discretion and judgment.
summary: TE Tolivar Wills complained that Metro Atlanta Presbytery improperly dissolved Grace North Atlanta Church without following formal judicial process under BCO 40-6. The SJC denied the complaint, ruling that BCO 13-9(f) grants presbytery inherent authority to dissolve a church without mandating any specific procedure, and that the record did not demonstrate clear error in MAP's exercise of its discretion and judgment.

title: Bachmann v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Bachmann appealed Nashville Presbytery's decision to amend its judicial commission's recommended censure of admonition to indefinite suspension; the SJC sustained the appeal, finding NP violated BCO 15-3 by dividing the question and amending the JC's judgment, and rendered the decision that should have been rendered by restoring the JC's censure of admonition.

title: Sartorius v. Siouxlands Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Sartorius complained that Siouxlands Presbytery erred in acquitting TE Greg Lawrence on five charges of holding Federal Vision and non-confessional views on baptism, perseverance, and covenant of works at a second trial (2015); the SJC denied the complaint 22-1, holding that the complainant failed to demonstrate clear error in the trial court's factual finding and that BCO 39-3.2 requires great deference to the lower court's verdict. A concurring opinion by RE Donahoe extensively discussed standards of appellate review, defendant testimony supporting the acquittal, and raised concerns about due process rights of acquitted persons.

title: Webster & Fowler v. Heritage Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: RE Webster and RE Fowler complained that Heritage Presbytery exceeded its authority when it passed a motion advising the Session of New Covenant Presbyterian Church to postpone ordaining a candidate who might be found unqualified due to non-subscription to infant baptism; the SJC denied the complaint 20-0, finding that Presbytery merely offered advice that Session was free to reject and did not impinge on Session's constitutional authority.
topic_tags: fundamentals of the system of doctrine

title: Dailey v. Heritage Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: RE Dailey complained that Heritage Presbytery erred in upholding its Moderator's ruling that a church member's document was administratively in order as a complaint under BCO 43-3, after the Session had ruled it out of order. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that neither triggering condition of BCO 43-3 was met because the Session's ruling that the document did not qualify as a BCO 43-1 complaint was not equivalent to denying it, and the Session had considered and responded to the matter in a timely manner. A substantial dissent argued for a broader interpretation of 'fails to consider' in BCO 43-3.

title: Postles v. Heritage Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: RE Postles complained that Heritage Presbytery erred in acting on an ad interim committee recommendation to charge a teaching elder with violating ordination vows 6 and 7 and appointing a prosecutor. The SJC denied the complaint, finding that a committee may recommend judicial action without special authorization (distinguishing from a commission under BCO 15-3), that BCO 31-2 procedures were properly followed, and that the language used by Presbytery in its motion was constitutionally sufficient to institute process.

title: Daniels et al. v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The 46th General Assembly record listed Daniels et al.’s complaint against Nashville Presbytery as out of order. The sparse published record does not identify the challenged action, specify an administrative or judicial subtype, provide a reason, or decide the merits.

title: BCO 40-5 report of RE John B. Thompson
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The 2017-04 BCO 40-5 report of RE John B. Thompson was withdrawn in the 46th General Assembly (2018) record, and no separate merits opinion was published. The available record states no underlying facts, issues, adopted reasons, or relief; it supplies only the docket disposition of the report.

title: BCO 40-5 Report of TE James Bachmann
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC docket records TE James Bachmann's BCO 40-5 report as out of order. The published record does not identify the procedural defect, describe the underlying allegations, or decide whether an important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceeding occurred.

title: Request for Reference from Blue Ridge Presbytery
disposition_detail: reference denied; complaint returned to presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Blue Ridge Presbytery asked the SJC to hear and decide a complaint by reference. The SJC denied the request because the record demonstrated neither presbytery-wide disqualification nor serious division, constitutional questions, or new, delicate, or difficult issues warranting reference. Presbytery therefore had to hear and decide the complaint itself. The ruling concerned only the proper court for adjudication and did not decide the complaint’s merits; companion case 2017-07 was answered by reference to this decision.

title: Clements v. Blue Ridge Presbytery (Complaint)
disposition_detail: reference denied; complaint returned to presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Blue Ridge Presbytery sought to have the SJC decide Clements’s complaint rather than hear it locally. Answering the complaint by reference to companion case 2017-06, the SJC directed Presbytery to hear and decide it because the record did not establish bias, serious division, constitutional questions, or unusually difficult issues warranting reference under BCO 41. The ruling did not decide the complaint’s merits.

title: BCO 40-5 report of RE John B. Thompson. Ruled
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: BCO 40-5 report of RE John B. Thompson listed in SJC docket as ruled out of order. No full opinion published.

title: BCO 40-5 report of RE John B. Thompson. Ruled
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The 46th General Assembly ruled the BCO 40-5 report of RE John B. Thompson out of order. The published record does not describe the report’s allegations, specify an administrative or judicial subtype, or provide reasons or a separate merits opinion.

title: In re Korean Eastern Presbytery

standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.

Compliance with the production requirement did not itself constitute substantive approval of the submitted records.

title: In re Korean Southwest Presbytery
disposition_detail: Citation responses accepted and forwarded to the Review of Presbytery Records Committee
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC accepted Korean Southwest Presbytery's responses, approved by the Presbytery, as complying with its citation. It forwarded them to the Review of Presbytery Records Committee. The sparse record identifies no underlying citation grounds, merits analysis, or separate opinion; the practical result was a finding of citation compliance and continued records review.

disposition_detail: Citation responses accepted and forwarded to the Review of Presbytery Records Committee

summary: The SJC unanimously accepted Platte Valley Presbytery's responses, which the Presbytery had approved, as complying with the SJC's citation. It noted that those responses and the requested minutes were forwarded to the Committee on Review of Presbytery Records. The entry does not disclose the underlying citation grounds or evaluate the presbytery's records on the merits; it confirms citation compliance and sends the materials on for ordinary records review.

title: Tripp v. Ohio Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: Withdrawn before decision; no merits disposition
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: TE David Tripp’s appeal against Ohio Valley Presbytery was withdrawn before the SJC issued a decision. No opinion text or merits disposition is recorded in the official case listing.

title: Glen Mapes v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained in part; censures reversed and replaced with admonition; related complaint moot
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: A ruling elder appealed convictions and censures arising from his brief refusal to leave a closed Temporary Session meeting. The SJC affirmed only his conviction for failing to submit to church government, because he knowingly attended and his apology acknowledged fault; it reversed findings of dereliction, sedition, rioting, and the balance for lack of supporting evidence. It rejected his first four appeal specifications, but held suspension and deposition excessive, substituted Admonition, and restored both sacraments and office, although he belonged to no particular Session.

title: Anna Lewis v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
disposition_detail: BCO 40-5 filing found out of order because Chapter 40 matters reach the SJC only upon General Assembly referral
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: After her session erased her from the roll, Anna Lewis filed a BCO 40-5 report directly with the SJC, alleging the Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley failed to redress the session's alleged failure to give BCO 38-4 notice. The SJC held the filing out of order: under RAO 16-10.c and OMSJC Chapter 15, BCO Chapter 40 matters come to it only by General Assembly referral. It did not decide the merits, but noted that without proper notice Lewis remains a member unless she joined another church. Dissents disputed that limitation and cited past direct reviews.

title: Durand v. Central Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC considered whether it could receive directly a BCO 31-2 report affecting Christian character. It ruled the matter administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because no constitutional provision authorizes such direct receipt. The order did not address the report’s substance or direct further proceedings.

title: Mapes v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint by RE Glen Mapes et al. not judicially in order because it was rendered moot: the remedy sought (a congregational meeting to vote on leaving the PCA) was accomplished when the presbytery voted to dismiss the congregation and the congregation consented. Three members dissented.

title: McKay v. Central Indiana Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC unanimously ruled the complaint by TE David McKay was administratively out of order because the e-mail transmitted to the clerk of the lower court did not meet BCO 43-3's requirement for proper notice.

title: Edwards v. North Texas Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled the complaint by Jared Edwards was administratively out of order and could not be put in order because the case was never filed with the presbytery or adjudicated below, as required by BCO 42-4 and 43-2.

title: Dodson et al. v. Ohio Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint partially sustained; further proceedings moot
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Grace PCA’s Session challenged Ohio Presbytery’s reversal of excommunication for two members convicted of heresy. The SJC partially sustained the complaint: prior indefinite suspension was not constitutionally required, but Presbytery properly found excommunication too severe because the trial record contained no evidence of contumacy. Presbytery nevertheless had to impose an appropriate lesser censure or remand for one, and lacked authority to mandate transfer to another church. The unappealed heresy convictions remained, but because the members had joined another church, further proceedings were moot.

title: Schrock et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Daniel Schrock and others complained that Philadelphia Presbytery failed to properly judge and record the nature of TE Larry Smith's views on the continuation of spiritual gifts of prophecy and tongues when it admitted him by transfer, as required by BCO 21-4e,f and RAO 16-3.e.5. The SJC sustained the complaint by a vote of 14-5-2 and remanded the matter to Presbytery to receive a written statement from TE Smith and make a proper determination, with a substantial dissent arguing the Presbytery had in fact complied with the Constitution and that RAO 16-3.e.5 is not part of the BCO.
topic_tags: fundamentals of the system of doctrine

title: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: A serving deacon nominated for ruling elder complained that his session removed his nomination before BCO 24-1 instruction or examination. The SJC held the session erred by adding an unwritten pre-examination 'vetting' removal and that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred in approving it: BCO 24-1's sequence—instruction and examination before the session determines eligibility—is mandatory. The ruling reserved the session's sound discretion and the treatment of frivolous or clearly disqualified nominees. The complaint was sustained and remanded for adjudication consistent with the decision.

title: Williams v. Chesapeake Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; Presbytery's approval annulled; matter returned to the PJC, which may dismiss or proceed under BCO 32
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: An indicted teaching elder challenged Chesapeake Presbytery’s approval of a PJC judgment and indefinite suspension after the PJC blended a BCO 32 case of process with a BCO 38-1 case without process. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s approval, and returned the matter to the PJC. Because he admitted only some indicted charges, his negotiated confession could not satisfy BCO 38-1 and the conversion prejudiced his rights. The PJC may dismiss or proceed under BCO 32; the ruling does not decide whether conversion is ever permissible.
topic_tags: case of process vs case without process

title: Goggan v. Missouri Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: An excommunicated member appealed the Missouri Presbytery judicial commission's guilty verdict and excommunication, alleging specifications of error. The SJC denied the appeal and did not sustain any specification, holding only that the appellant failed to demonstrate sufficient reason to sustain the alleged errors; the excommunication thus remained in effect. The record noted Presbytery dismissed the commission without the BCO 15-3 vote to approve its report, but the adopted reasoning gave no further explanation and did not address that fact.

title: Presbyterian Church in America v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings.; BCO 39-3.4: the higher court interprets and applies the Church Constitution according to its best ability, without the same deference to the lower court.
summary: In a BCO 40-5 matter, the SJC held that a presbytery erred in upholding a session's erasure of a member who pled not guilty to failing to submit and pursued divorce. The session wrongly equated declining divorce counsel with refusing submission, failed to assess membership duties in another branch, failed to notify her of erasure, and proceeded without process after dropping charges. The SJC sustained the challenge, directed the session to note the notice failure and remove her under BCO 38-3(a), but ordered no express reversal.

title: Fozard v. North Texas Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Mr. Chandler Fozard complained that Fort Worth Presbyterian Church's policy restricting the integration of special case felons (including sex offenders) into the congregation violated Scripture. The SJC denied the complaint 20-1, finding the complainant had not demonstrated the Session violated Scripture or the Constitution, while criticizing the Session's arguments from BCO Preliminary Principles 1 and 2 as improper.

title: Ganzel v. Central Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A minister appealed a judgment finding him guilty on most charges and imposing six months’ suspension. The SJC held BCO 32-20 barred Specifications 1, 2, and 4 because Presbytery lacked extraordinary justification for prosecuting old allegations, but did not bar ongoing Specification 3. It separately found the entire process constitutionally flawed and prejudicial. The SJC reversed the whole censure, declined Presbytery’s requested harsher sentence, and concluded the matter. A concurrence disputed the majority’s BCO 32-20 interpretation while agreeing with the result.

title: Mueller v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: RE Mueller complained that the Redlands Community Church Session reaffirmed a practice of fencing the Lord's Table contrary to BCO 58-4, but the SJC found the Session took no action because the relevant motion failed for lack of a second. The complaint was denied, with a concurring opinion emphasizing that BCO 58-4's fencing requirement remains a constitutional obligation.

title: Evans and Pitts et al. v. Arizona Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Arizona Presbytery deposed TE John Evans without process after considering investigative-committee observations he had not approved. The SJC sustained the joined complaints, annulled the deposition, and remanded. BCO 38-1 requires the accused and court to approve one full statement of facts; Evans could not approve facts presented after he left. But the provision does not expressly require a meeting or detailed discussion. The underlying matter remained unresolved: Presbytery could proceed with or without process, or dismiss it.

title: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The adopted opinion applies BCO 39-3.3 to the Session's exercise of discretion and judgment; the dissent argues for BCO 39-3.4 but does not alter the majority holding.
summary: The SJC denied a complaint by an ordained Deacon whose nomination for re-election was not advanced by the Session, holding that the Session's exercise of discretion in evaluating a candidate's eligibility for office did not constitute clear error requiring reversal. The dissent argued the proper standard of review was BCO 39-3.4 (de novo for constitutional interpretation), not 39-3.3 (great deference), because the Session applied extra-biblical and extra-constitutional attendance standards in blocking re-election.

title: Gendy v. Central Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A member removed from the rolls under BCO 38-4 challenged Presbytery's ruling that she lacked standing to complain because she was no longer a member. The SJC sustained the complaint: standing under BCO 43-1 cannot be defeated by the very removal challenged. Removal under BCO 38-4 is pastoral discipline, a disciplinary case, not a merely administrative act. The SJC remanded to Presbytery to consider the complaint and take the action it should have taken—remand to the Session. The merits of the removal were not decided.

title: Yoo et al. v. Korean Southwest Orange County Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found this complaint administratively out of order and dismissed it because no documentation was received showing the complaint was first made to the presbytery whose act was alleged to be in error, and the proper court for the charges included was the Presbytery.

title: In the matter of PCA v. Missouri Presbytery
disposition_detail: BCO 34-1 requests answered by reference to Cases 2020-12 and 2020-05
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC answered three presbyteries' BCO 34-1 requests concerning Missouri Presbytery by reference to two Speck complaint decisions. One had upheld Missouri's decision not to indict on four allegations; the other had partly sustained a procedural and supervisory complaint and ordered a focused new hearing. The brief ruling gave no separate judgment or reasoning on the original-jurisdiction requests and did not transfer them to another court.

title: Marusich v. Central Indiana Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint returned to Central Indiana Presbytery with instructions to reinvestigate under BCO 31-2
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Marusich challenged Presbytery’s receipt of a commission’s finding that accusations against a teaching elder did not establish a strong presumption of guilt, and the commission’s failure to provide minutes or a full report. Without answering either issue or identifying an error, the SJC remanded for a new BCO 31-2 investigation, a narrative of the evidence, and a recommendation for Presbytery’s consideration under regular orders. The decision expressly establishes no general rule for BCO 31-2 investigations.

title: Speck v. Missouri Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The adopted opinion resolves the complaint on the constitutional criteria and procedural errors identified, without stating a distinct BCO 39-3 standard of review.
summary: Speck challenged Missouri Presbytery’s approval of six theological judgments concerning teachings at Revoice 18, its rejection of his procedural point of order, and its refusal to debate gay-couple adoption. The SJC sustained only the first issue, particularly as to Judgments 2, 3, and 5: Presbytery improperly imported BCO 34-5’s ministerial-process standard into court review and then inadequately addressed identified errors affecting church peace and purity. It rejected the procedural and adoption claims and remanded for a focused new hearing under BCO 11-3, 11-4, and 13-9(f).

title: Gordon v. Southern New England Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A church member appealed Presbytery’s affirmance of his conviction and excommunication for failing to heed Session admonition and membership vows, including prolonged absence from that church. The SJC affirmed and denied the appeal, holding that all four specifications—lack of reasonable indulgence, haste, prejudice, and injustice—were nonspecific and unsupported. It emphasized his admissions that the charges were true, the adequate timeline, and the bar on considering evidence not offered at trial. A dissent disputed his PCA membership, standing, and the Session’s jurisdiction.

title: Wilbourne v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Pacific Presbytery allowed its Judicial Commission to read a six-page adverse report containing new assertions beyond TE Rankin Wilbourne's agreed BCO 38-1 confession, then ruled his sins "base and flagitious" and deposed him. The SJC sustained his complaint and annulled the deposition, holding BCO 38-1 barred the prejudicial report and BCO 34-7 did not apply without a pending trial. It recommended treating the 17-month censure as sufficient definite suspension, restoring ministerial standing without call, and closing the matter; dissolution of his call was not annulled.

title: Gendall, Hightower, and Lien v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Three Teaching Elders complained against Pacific Presbytery's handling of TE Wilbourne's BCO 38-1 confession and subsequent deposition. The SJC sustained the complaints by reference to its decision in Case 2020-07.

title: Oxbalt et al. v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Pacific Crossroads Church’s Session challenged Presbytery’s handling of a minister’s BCO 38-1 confession, particularly its hearing an adverse investigative report outside the agreed statement before imposing deposition. The SJC sustained Case 2020-09 by reference to its consolidated decision and annulled the deposition: BCO 38-1 permits censure to rest only on the mutually approved statement, not additional adverse material. It recommended treating the elapsed 17 months as definite suspension and closing the matter. The minister returned to good standing without call; dissolution of his call remained intact.

title: Eagle v. Savannah River Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled Case 2020-10 administratively out of order as prematurely filed because Presbytery had not yet completed its hearing on the complaint; the complainant's time to elevate was reset.

title: McWilliams v. Southwest Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The complaint against Southwest Florida Presbytery ended when the SJC approved Complainant David McWilliams's request to withdraw and abandon it, by unanimous roll-call vote (24-0-0) on March 25, 2021. The adopted decision recites no underlying dispute, merits analysis, or reasons and makes no substantive ruling; the complaint stands withdrawn and abandoned. The sparse record is useful only as an example of an approved pre-decision withdrawal/abandonment.

title: Speck v. Missouri Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint denied; all stated issues answered no
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Ryan Speck challenged Missouri Presbytery’s BCO 31-2 investigation and its refusal to commence process against Greg Johnson on four allegations concerning same-sex attraction as sin, identity in Christ, sanctification, and fitness for office. The SJC denied the complaint in full. It found no clear procedural error and held that Johnson’s explanations and clarifications made Presbytery’s non-indictment judgments reasonable. No trial was ordered. The ruling neither adjudged Johnson guilty nor endorsed every statement or broader constitutional position concerning same-sex attraction.

title: Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed this complaint as administratively out of order because Mr. Benyola lacked standing to complain against a presbytery action, as he was neither a teaching elder member of that presbytery nor a ruling elder commissioner representing a member church at the September 18, 2020 meeting where the presbytery considered and denied the complaint.

title: Michelson v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled Case 2021-01 administratively out of order as prematurely filed because Presbytery had not yet completed its hearing on the complaint; the complainant's time to elevate was reset.

title: Tippins v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: In this BCO 40-5 request, the SJC advised the Stated Clerk that Tippins v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery should be referred to the General Assembly's Review of Presbytery Records Committee. The SJC approved that action 19-3-0; three commissioners dissented. The sparse record supplies no underlying facts, merits analysis, or reason for the referral.

title: DeJong v. Session of Village Seven Presbyterian Church
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A ruling elder challenged Session’s elder-term proposal and its creation of Judicial and Governance Commissions. The SJC denied the first two claims: the Constitution does not regulate elder terms, and the Judicial Commission’s assigned business was sufficiently defined. It sustained the Governance Commission claim because sweeping authority and reversed delegation allowed that body to function as Session itself, contrary to BCO 15-1. Session’s third motion was annulled, but Session remained free to adopt a narrower, constitutionally compliant plan.

title: Eudaly and Light v. Southwest Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled Case 2021-05 administratively out of order because the complainants had affiliated with another branch of the visible church on February 9, 2020, losing PCA jurisdiction and therefore lacking standing to file the complaint.

title: Herron et al. v. Central Indiana Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Herron and others challenged Presbytery’s decision to proceed to trial after a BCO 31-2 finding, his administrative suspension, denial of access to Presbytery records and meetings, and a public statement. The SJC sustained only the access issue: suspension from official functions did not remove his membership rights, though it did not entitle him to every investigative-committee document. Finding no clear error on the other issues, it ordered trial to proceed, temporarily stayed censure decisions, and postponed related complaints through trial and any appeal.

title: RE J. Lance Acree v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because Acree lacked standing under BCO 43-1
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: RE Acree attempted to complain directly to Tennessee Valley Presbytery about action taken at a meeting where he was not a commissioner. The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because BCO 43-1 gave him no standing to complain against that action. It added that Presbytery should itself have declined to adjudicate the complaint.

title: In re Korean Southwest Orange County Presbytery
disposition_detail: Citation and response process; no merits disposition in this record
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: As of March 3, 2022, Presbytery had not supplied formally adopted responses to records-review exceptions, although its clerk had prepared drafts. The SJC allowed time for adoption and filing by April 1, after which it would forward the responses for records review; failure to file would prompt a called hearing. This was an unfinished compliance process, not approval of the draft responses or a final merits decision.

title: Park et al. v. Korean Central Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Teaching elders challenged Korean Central Presbytery’s summary censure of a minister before an indictment was prepared. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s action because discipline preceded particular charges and a specific confession, and because an independent church lacked authority to impose PCA censure. It declared the underlying matter moot because the alleged event was twenty-one years old and the victim would not cooperate, ending the proceeding without remand. The ruling addressed neither the allegations’ merits nor all old charges categorically.

title: Michelson v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order because it targeted actions of a congregational meeting rather than any act or decision of a court of the Church, as required by BCO 43-1. A dissenting opinion by RE Jack Wilson and seven others argued that the Complainants had sufficiently identified an act of the Session (calling the congregational meeting with the stated purposes) to present a justiciable issue.
topic_tags: BCO 43-1 act or decision of a court

title: Dudt v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: A ruling elder appealed convictions for distributing an SJC decision contrary to Session's will and for allegedly false, divisive statements in an email opposing a pastoral-election proposal. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversed Session and Presbytery in whole, rendered not guilty, removed the indefinite suspension, and restored him to office. Session could not bind conscience without scriptural authority, and no express prohibition or proof of falsity existed. Many other specifications were rejected; a concurrence cautioned that such emails are rarely wise.
topic_tags: express vs. implied will of session

title: Herron et al. v. Central Indiana Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Herron challenged Presbytery's handling of its directive that he withdraw his civil defamation lawsuit. The SJC answered the complaint by reference to its completed trial decision in 2022-10, which acquitted him on all seven charges, removed all censures and administrative suspensions, and restored him to ministerial good standing. The incorporated decision found the lawsuit's sinfulness unproved; the complaint notice supplied no separate issue-by-issue ruling.

title: Barber et al. v. Central Indiana Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Barber and others challenged Presbytery's actions rescinding Herron's contumacy judgment. The SJC answered their complaint by reference to its completed trial decision in 2022-10, which acquitted Herron on all seven charges, removed all censures and administrative suspensions, and restored him to ministerial good standing. That decision found the lawsuit's sinfulness unproved, undermining the related contumacy charge. The complaint notice supplied no separate issue-by-issue ruling.

title: Eagle v. Savannah River Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Complaint by Eric Eagle and others against Savannah River Presbytery, found administratively out of order by the SJC Officers because the complaint was not timely filed within thirty days of the later of the SJC's notification (October 21, 2021) or Presbytery's ruling (October 20, 2020), as required by BCO 43-3. The case was dismissed on a unanimous 19-0-0 vote.

title: Herron & Baysinger v. Central Indiana Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC answered this Herron-related complaint by reference to its final decision in the Herron trial, which acquitted him on all seven charges, removed all censures and administrative suspensions imposed by Presbytery, and restored his good standing as a minister. The complaint notice supplies no separate ruling on its individual allegations.

title: Klett et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC sustained a complaint against Philadelphia Presbytery for failing to find that TE Larry Smith's views affirming continuing gifts of prophecy and tongues (as a 'third category of revelation' beyond special and general revelation) were out of accord with the fundamentals of the system of doctrine because hostile to it, as required by BCO 21-4.f. The case continues past this window's end page.
