fundamentals of the system of doctrine

title: Sheppard v. Highlands Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: TE Craig Sheppard complained that Highlands Presbytery erred by conflating judicial and pastoral procedures after finding a strong presumption of guilt, and by failing to institute process within one year as required by BCO 32-20. The SJC sustained both issues, holding that BCO 31-2 mandates process upon finding a strong presumption of guilt, and that Presbytery was debarred from prosecution because the alleged offense occurred in 2017 and timely process was never instituted; three members dissented on the BCO 32-20 issue, arguing it was not a true statute of limitations and that the matter was never a 'case of scandal.'

title: Crouse et al. v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint out of order and moot
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Three Ruling Elders complained of errors in judicial process against them. The SJC found the complaint out of order and moot because the Session had dismissed every charge and ended the process, while the elders had voluntarily resigned and requested dissolution of their calls. Because these events removed the challenged action and settled the underlying dispute, the SJC did not reach the alleged procedural errors.

title: Biese et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The Complainants withdrew this Complaint on July 18, 2022, and the SJC noted such on October 20, 2022. No substantive decision was issued.

title: Harrell et al. v. Covenant Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Seven members of a PCA mission church were tried and censured by a provisional Session for opposing the organizing minister's continuation as permanent pastor. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the convictions, holding that the indictments lacked required specificity under BCO 32-5, that the accused had no sinned against the fifth or ninth commandment by expressing opinions about ministerial suitability, and that the right to choose a pastor belongs to the congregation—not the provisional Session. A concurring opinion addressed indictment requirements, standard of review in appeals, and congregational rights in mission church minister selection.

title: David Snoke v. Pittsburgh Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order and unable to be put in order because RE Snoke lacked standing to file a complaint against presbytery action, as he was not a commissioner from his church to the presbytery meeting where the challenged action occurred. The SJC voted 20-1 to dismiss (Sartorius dissenting).

title: Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order because Mr. Benyola was no longer a member of any PCA congregation and thus lacked standing. The SJC approved the dismissal unanimously 23-0.

title: Presbyterian Church in America v. TE Daniel Herron
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: On a BCO 41 reference, the SJC tried a minister on seven charges arising from allegations of sexual misconduct, bullying, dishonesty, a civil defamation suit, contumacy, doctrinal error, and lack of fitness. It found him not guilty on every charge because the prosecution failed to meet its burden, removed all censures and administrative suspensions, and restored him to good standing. For the lawsuit charge, it rejected a categorical ban on civil suits between Christians and required proof that this suit was sinful.

title: BCO 34-1 Petitions re: Central Indiana Presbytery
disposition_detail: BCO 34-1 petitions answered and decided by reference to the final decision in Case 2022-10
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC had postponed BCO 34-1 petitions concerning Central Indiana Presbytery until the Herron trial concluded. After acquitting Herron on all charges and restoring him to good standing, the SJC answered and decided the petitions by reference to that final trial decision. The petitions were thus resolved through incorporation of the trial result, not transferred to another court; the trial itself arose from a distinct BCO 41 reference.

title: BCO 34-1 Petitions re: Missouri Presbytery
disposition_detail: BCO 34-1 petitions dismissed for lack of jurisdiction after the minister and congregation left the PCA
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Two overtures from Southeast Alabama and Grace Presbyteries sought GA assumption of original jurisdiction over TE Greg Johnson of Missouri Presbytery for alleged doctrinal errors; the SJC dismissed the petitions (22-1) because TE Johnson and Memorial Presbyterian Church withdrew from the PCA in December 2022, depriving the PCA of jurisdiction.

title: Miller v. Hills & Plains Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found Mr. Miller's complaint administratively out of order (22-0) because he filed it with the Session six months after the Session's action (May 19, 2021), well beyond the 60-day deadline required by BCO 43-1.

title: Oh v. Korean Southeast Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint withdrawn; dismissed without merits decision
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed Oh’s complaint against Korean Southeast Presbytery following his withdrawal of it. The brief decision does not identify the challenged presbytery action, address the merits, or grant substantive relief.

title: Murdock v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order (23-0) because complainant RE Terry Murdock died on November 15, 2022, and no other party had joined the original complaint.

title: Michelson et al. v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint out of order and moot (23-0) because the Session had dismissed all charges against the three Ruling Elders involved and those REs voluntarily resigned and had their calls dissolved on July 23, 2022, settling the underlying dispute.

title: Peter Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery (three complaints)
disposition_detail: Complaints administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order for lack of standing
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Peter Benyola's three complaints against Central Florida Presbytery were found administratively out of order because he was no longer a member of a PCA congregation and therefore lacked standing; the SJC did not reach the merits.

title: Wilson et al. v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Members challenged a voting restriction imposed at a congregational meeting. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order because BCO 43-1 permits complaints against acts or decisions of church courts, and a congregation is not such a court. It identified other possible routes through a report to Presbytery or review of church records. The adopted decision did not decide whether the voting restriction was constitutionally valid.

title: Senters v. Savannah River Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A minister challenged Presbytery’s procedures and its classification of a transfer candidate’s views on continuing tongues as “not a difference.” The SJC rejected the procedural objections because Presbytery could disregard its committee’s recommendation and had breached no required procedure. It nevertheless held that a difference need not overtly contradict the Standards and that the candidate’s statements implicated WCF 1.1 and 1.6. It annulled the classification and remanded for clarification and a new judgment, without deciding whether the clarified view would be acceptable.

title: Turner v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: Issue 1 denied; Issue 2 sustained; findings of guilt and censures annulled; matter returned to South Florida Presbytery for constitutionally appropriate proceedings
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Presbytery investigated a Session's handling of sexual-misconduct allegations and found it guilty of delinquencies without a trial. The SJC upheld Presbytery's authority to receive credible reports and investigate, but annulled the findings of guilt, censures, and corrective mandates because BCO 40-6 required formal process or an admission before censure. It returned the matter for records review, informal resolution, or formal process and declined interim mandates that would assume the disputed allegations were true.

title: Woodham v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: TE Michael Woodham complained that South Florida Presbytery erred by excommunicating a Teaching Elder it had previously deposed without first assigning him to membership in a particular church as required by BCO 46-8. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that Presbytery retained jurisdiction over a deposed minister until transfer to a local church was completed, and that Presbytery's efforts to implement BCO 46-8 showed no clear error; two concurring opinions (RE Donahoe and RE Eggert) offered alternative reasoning regarding the scope of Presbytery's residual jurisdiction.

title: Hann v. Pee Dee Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed Mrs. Hann's complaint against Pee Dee Presbytery because she lacked standing, not being subject to the jurisdiction of the Presbytery. The ruling noted that Presbytery's ongoing investigation was not stayed by this ruling.
topic_tags: complainant not subject to presbytery jurisdiction

title: Reynolds v. Pee Dee Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed Mrs. Reynolds's complaint against Pee Dee Presbytery as untimely, finding it was filed more than sixty days after the Session action in question. The ruling expressly reserved questions about whether she might bring charges as an injured party under BCO 31-5.

title: Biese et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Biese and others complained that Tennessee Valley Presbytery erred by approving Redeemer Church session minutes without exception—minutes noting a youth Super Bowl party—and by denying their complaint seeking a Sabbath exception. The SJC denied the complaint: because Presbytery gave no reasons for its actions, the record was insufficient to find it erred in interpreting the Constitution. A concurrence said the denial did not decide the Sabbath merits; a dissent would have held the complaint judicially out of order for lack of SJC jurisdiction over presbytery record review.

title: Hyland v. Chicago Metro Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A terminated church employee filed a complaint against Chicago Metro Presbytery after Presbytery declined to indict the pastors she accused, but Presbytery ruled her complaint out of order for lack of standing under BCO 43-1. The SJC, voting 12-12, left the Presbytery's decision standing, finding the complaint judicially out of order because the complainant lacked standing to file a BCO 43-1 complaint against Presbytery.

title: Knox Baird et al. v. Grace Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaints sustained in the main; one specification denied and one not reached
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Session elders challenged Presbytery’s handling of a mediation complaint, investigative directives, BCO 40-5 reports, and a trial stay. The SJC held that the mediation complaint was never formally filed and became moot; official-record requests were proper, but compelling nonrecord personal communications and requiring the Session to address its congregation exceeded Presbytery’s authority. It vacated the communications directive and annulled the stay for lack of the required prior citation. It upheld committee examination of the BCO 40-5 reports and did not reach alleged partiality; the Session trials were to proceed.

title: Evans v. Arizona Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Arizona Presbytery divested a minister without censure for prolonged lack of call after he had joined an EPCEW congregation and notified Presbytery of his withdrawal. The SJC sustained his appeal and reversed the divestiture because BCO 38-3(a) had already ended Presbytery's jurisdiction while he was in good standing and under no investigation or charges. It directed Presbytery to record the irregular withdrawal, acknowledge his new membership, and remove him from its roll.

title: Knox Baird et al. v. Grace Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaints sustained in the main; one specification denied and one not reached
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Session elders challenged Presbytery’s handling of a withdrawn mediation complaint, document and congregational-notice directives, BCO 40-5 reports, and a stay of Session trials. The SJC sustained the complaints in the main: the mediation complaint was never formally filed and became moot; Presbytery could require official record materials but not compel personal communications or force the Session to address its congregation; and the stay lacked a prior BCO 40-5 citation. It upheld appointing a committee to examine the reports, did not reach alleged partiality, vacated the overbroad directive, annulled the stay, and returned the trials to Session.

title: Myers v. Illiana Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained 21-1; Presbytery's action reversed in whole and prior suspensions restored pending constitutionally adequate process
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: An elder appealed Presbytery’s elevation, without additional process, of suspensions from office and the Sacraments to deposition and excommunication. The SJC granted the appeal, reversed in whole, and remanded, restoring the prior suspensions. Elevation required a hearing on incorrigibility and contumacy—with a charge, evidence, plea, and defense—but not a full de novo trial; disagreement with the original verdict alone was insufficient. The SJC left unresolved deposition from office when excommunication is absent.

title: Martinez & Cook v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Elders challenged Presbytery’s authority and vague instruction for its Shepherding Committee to “follow up” with their Session. The SJC denied the constitutional challenge because the record reasonably supported concern for the church’s peace and spiritual welfare, but sustained the challenge to Presbytery’s lack of specific direction and poor communication. The decision distinguishes prohibited mandatory visitation without cause from a reasonably justified visit, while requiring clarity about its objectives. It did not decide the underlying doxology dispute or order further relief.

title: Psiaki v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC sustained Psiaki’s complaint and held that the CPC Session erred by ordaining and installing officers elected at a February 5, 2023 congregational meeting where the congregation’s bylaw excluded communing members under 18 from voting. Reading BCO 6-4, 25-1, and 25-7 together, the SJC ruled that all communing members are entitled to vote and that local bylaws cannot impose an age restriction; the “good and regular standing” language addresses censure, not age. The decision did not annul the completed ordination/installation, but required future elections and installations to comply with the Constitution.

title: BCO 40-5 Matter re Metropolitan NY
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: A BCO 40-5 citation arose from Metro New York Presbytery's failure to redress a session that allowed a woman to expound Scripture in place of the sermon preceding the Lord's Supper, held services without preaching, and celebrated the Supper without a preceding sermon. The SJC remitted the matter to the presbytery for constitutional resolution because the session's later no-exception response was clearly inadequate and the unapproved minutes were unclear. Presbytery must complete its work with TE Higgins and Trinity Presbyterian Church's session and report to the 51st General Assembly. A separate procedural note questioned the Assembly's direct referral but did not void it.

title: BCO 40-5 Matter re NW Georgia
disposition_detail: BCO 40-5 ruling found egregious constitutional error and fully redressed the reported matter, but denied the requested annulment of the installations.
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings; the SJC found egregious constitutional error and addressed the requested relief.
summary: Presbytery approved calls and installed three associate pastors after a constitutionally deficient election. The SJC found egregious error, including slate voting, a standing rather than ballot vote, and failure to determine and record the number of voters present under the then-current rule. It nevertheless denied the requested annulment of the installations because PCA judicial proceedings supplied no precedent and the remedy's legitimacy was doubtful. The SJC stayed further proceedings and declared the report concluded.

title: Tom Turner v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: Administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order for lack of standing
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Turner complained against Presbytery Judicial Commission actions deposing TE Tommy Boland and dissolving Cross Community Church’s relationship with Presbytery. The SJC ruled both complaints administratively out of order for lack of standing and incapable of being put in order. Cross Community had already disaffiliated through its first congregational motion; the second motion, which contemplated later implementation, was out of order as contingent. Because no Presbytery action was required to effect disaffiliation, Turner was no longer a PCA member. The underlying challenges were not decided.

title: Tom Turner v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: Administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order for lack of standing
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Turner’s two complaints challenged the deposition of TE Tommy Boland and the dissolution of Cross Community Church’s relationship with Presbytery, although the record does not identify which challenge was Case 2023-17. In a combined ruling, the SJC held both complaints administratively out of order for lack of standing. The congregation’s first withdrawal vote immediately satisfied BCO 25-11; its second, contingent timing motion was out of order. Because the church had already left the PCA, Turner was no longer a member, and no merits relief was available.

title: Huffman v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: A filing challenging Presbytery’s handling of Huffman’s BCO 38-1 confession was styled as an appeal under a newly amended rule. The SJC found it judicially out of order because the case began and was nearly completed when the former rule provided review by complaint, and retroactive application would be unfair. It remanded for Presbytery to adjudicate the filing as a complaint at its next stated meeting; denial or failure to act permits review by the SJC. No merits issue was decided.

title: Felipe Assis and Carter Brown v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained; divestitures reversed and both ministers restored to good standing
standard_of_review_detail: The SJC held that Presbytery clearly erred in judgment and acted unconstitutionally under BCO 34-10; it construed BCO 13-2 and 34-10 while declining to resolve disputed factual matters outside the record.
summary: Two ministers appealed Presbytery’s divestiture of their offices after their congregations left the PCA. The SJC reversed because their calls had never been formally dissolved, so they were not automatically without call, and BCO 34-10 did not apply while they remained actively engaged and accepted in ministry. The SJC could not judge their fairness and pretext claims from the record. It restored them to good standing and required Presbytery to dissolve the existing calls before pursuing lawful alternatives.

title: Felipe Assis and Carter Brown v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained; divestitures reversed and both ministers restored to good standing
standard_of_review_detail: The SJC held that Presbytery clearly erred in judgment and acted unconstitutionally under BCO 34-10; it construed BCO 13-2 and 34-10 while declining to resolve disputed factual matters outside the record.
summary: Two ministers appealed Presbytery’s decision to divest them of office without censure after their congregations left the PCA. The SJC sustained the BCO-violation specification and reversed the divestitures: their calls had never been formally dissolved, and BCO 34-10 did not apply because they continued performing ministerial functions and remained accepted by their churches. It declined as unable to judge claims that Presbytery disregarded their emails or used the procedure as discriminatory pretext. The ministers returned to good standing; Presbytery must dissolve their existing PCA calls and then pursue a BCO-consistent option.
